claims.statement: For every compact simple gauge group G, construct a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory satisfying the required axioms and prove a finite positive Hamiltonian mass gap.
claims.scope_and_quantifiers: All compact simple gauge groups; full continuum R^4; pure quantum Yang-Mills.
known_limitations: No construction or mass-gap proof is present in this repository.
falsification_tests: Audit any purported completion against every obligation in PROBLEM.md and STATUS.json.
open_objections: The complete official problem remains open.
claims.provenance: Official Clay target, paraphrased and scope-audited on 2026-07-22.

claims.statement: For a nonnegative self-adjoint Hamiltonian with one-dimensional vacuum kernel, a positive spectral gap Delta is equivalent to sufficiently-large-time Delta-rate exponential decay of the Euclidean semigroup quadratic form on a subspace dense in the vacuum-orthogonal sector, with vector-dependent finite onset time and prefactor; if that sector is nonzero, the supremal gap is finite.
claims.scope_and_quantifiers: Abstract Hilbert-space Hamiltonians; no Yang-Mills construction or regulator limit is assumed or proved.
external_hypotheses: Spectral theorem and Borel functional calculus for nonnegative self-adjoint operators.
known_limitations: The criterion does not construct a QFT.
It does not prove the required exponential estimate for Yang-Mills observables.
It does not transfer a regulator-dependent bound unless convergence and uniformity hypotheses are separately proved.
The result is elementary and no novelty is claimed.
falsification_tests: Check the argument for continuous spectrum accumulating at zero.
Check that density is used to eliminate a hidden low-energy spectral subspace.
Check that the vacuum atom is removed by orthogonality.
Test whether a prefactor depending on the state invalidates the large-time contradiction.
Check the one-dimensional vacuum-only case and the separate nontriviality condition needed for finite mass.
open_objections: No independent human review has been recorded.
claims.provenance: AI-assisted derivation, with the complete proof exposed for independent checking.

claims.statement: For an Osterwalder-Schrader reconstructed theory with unique vacuum, reflected centered correlations over a total nonvacuum family determine the bottom of the Hamiltonian spectrum; regulator correlations that converge at fixed physical time and satisfy a regulator- and volume-uniform epsilon-loss exponential bound imply a continuum gap.
claims.scope_and_quantifiers: Conditional OS-reconstructed theories and convergent regulator sequences; no Yang-Mills measure, convergence theorem, decay estimate, or OS axiom is established.
external_hypotheses: A limiting Schwinger functional satisfying corrected Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction hypotheses.
A unique reconstructed vacuum and a nontrivial vacuum-orthogonal sector.
Physical-time convergence of specified renormalized reflected correlations.
Totality of the limiting centered observable classes.
A regulator- and volume-uniform physical exponential estimate with arbitrary epsilon loss.
known_limitations: Every Yang-Mills-specific construction and estimate appears as an unproved hypothesis.
The corollary does not show that a proposed observable family is total.
It does not justify reflection positivity after gauge fixing or renormalization.
The result is an elementary conditional bridge and no novelty is claimed.
falsification_tests: Test a family that is not total and can miss a low-energy spectral sector.
Test a regulator-dependent prefactor that diverges before the fixed-time limit.
Check the order of the regulator, fixed-physical-time, and large-time limits.
Check that lattice-unit decay is converted using physical time a_r k.
Check the one-dimensional vacuum-only case and the separate nontriviality hypothesis.
open_objections: No independent human review has been recorded.
No Yang-Mills regulator sequence is known here to satisfy the hypotheses.
claims.provenance: AI-assisted conditional derivation from the spectral theorem and standard OS reconstruction identities; complete proof and quantifiers are exposed for audit.

claims.statement: For one gauge-covariant RG block step in four-dimensional SU(2) Wilson lattice gauge theory, derive a source-inserted local plaquette-energy decomposition with classified operator/profile mixing, gauge-invariant localized polymer remainders, volume-independent bounds through two source derivatives, explicit large-field control, and the raw coupling-derivative consistency identity.
claims.scope_and_quantifiers: One block factor; SU(2); a normalized compactly supported plaquette-energy profile class for local estimates plus a separate finite-volume constant profile used only at first derivative; no RG iteration, continuum limit, or infrared conclusion.
external_hypotheses: A still-to-be-pinned Bałaban gauge-covariant raw block transformation, its fine minimizing background, and every needed source-free small- and large-field estimate, each verified in full text before use.
known_limitations: This is an unproved theorem specification.
Even a proof would not construct the continuum theory or establish a mass gap.
Parts may already be implicit in Bałaban's work; no novelty is claimed.
falsification_tests: Reject omission of large fields or group cut-locus control.

Reject failure of coarse gauge invariance, source locality, a zero-free analytic disk, complete source-mixing classification, the raw-transform constant-source identity, volume-uniform first/second source-jet bounds, or the universal one-loop check.
open_objections: Exact block map, norms, and admissible field domains are not yet pinned.
The theorem may duplicate or fail to follow from existing source-free estimates.
The source-dependent extension of the separate large-field operation has not been derived.
claims.provenance: Research specification synthesized from the official problem and primary lattice/RG literature; no proof claimed.
